haiku-low.q1: Held 10 minutes in Inventory. If the hold expired, the claim reserves again if stock fits; if not, the order is cancelled and refunded.
haiku-low.q2: Reserved before the charge. If any line is short, nothing is saved, Order cancels with reason short stock, and no payment is requested.
haiku-low.q3: The order id is sent as the idempotency key. Order retries with the same order id, so the provider cannot charge twice.
haiku-low.q4: Order cancels with reason out of stock, emails the customer, and asks Payment to refund the full amount with the order id key.
haiku-low.q5: Cart is emptied on OrderConfirmed. Every failure before that leaves the cart unchanged.
haiku-low.q6: Order coordinates the flow and keeps the order status in its database: pending, confirmed or cancelled.
haiku-low.q7: The provider sends a webhook to Payment, which hosts the endpoint. Payment publishes the outcome as an event on the broker, which Order receives.
haiku-low.q8: Payment stores each processed event id, and a repeated event id does nothing.
haiku-low.q9: Payment publishes PaymentDeclined. Order cancels with reason payment declined, then asks Inventory to release the hold, which Inventory deletes.
haiku-low.q10: The claim decides: if the hold is active or stock fits again, Order confirms; otherwise Order cancels as out of stock and refunds.
haiku-low.q11: Payment retries the provider with the same key until accepted. The refund row stays pending in Payment's database and raises an alert.
haiku-low.q12: The OrderConfirmed event causes Cart to empty the cart. Emptying an empty cart does nothing.

sonnet.q1: Held for 10 minutes. If not claimed, the hold expires and the stock becomes free again (counted as free stock; lapsed hold). A late successful payment then triggers a re-reserve attempt of the same lines.
sonnet.q2: Stock is reserved before charging. If any line is short, nothing is saved/held, Order cancels with reason short stock, the customer is shown the short items, no payment is requested, and the cart is unchanged.
sonnet.q3: The order id is sent as the idempotency key, so a retry with the same key cannot charge twice.
sonnet.q4: Order is cancelled with reason out of stock and the customer is emailed. Order asks Payment to refund the full amount (refund row pending, provider called with order id as key, retried until accepted, then marked refunded). Customer sees 'cancelled, out of stock' until refund is accepted.
sonnet.q5: The cart is emptied only on OrderConfirmed (by Cart). On any failure before that, the cart is left unchanged.
sonnet.q6: Order coordinates the flow. The record of progress is the order status (pending, confirmed, cancelled, with reason) in Order's database; other services keep their own rows (hold, charge, refund). A pending order has no finer step-tracking stated.
sonnet.q7: The provider sends a webhook to an endpoint hosted by Payment. Payment stores the event id, sets the charge to succeeded/declined, and publishes PaymentSucceeded or PaymentDeclined on the broker. Order receives PaymentSucceeded (and handles PaymentDeclined) from the broker.
sonnet.q8: Payment stores processed event ids; if the event id is already stored it does nothing. Storing the id and updating the charge happen in one transaction. Also Order does nothing for an already confirmed order, and repeat claims return claimed.
sonnet.q9: PaymentDeclined triggers it: Order cancels the order (reason payment declined), then asks Inventory to release the hold (Inventory deletes the hold row). Order retries the release; if missed, the hold still expires after 10 minutes; release does nothing if the hold is already expired or never saved.
sonnet.q10: On PaymentSucceeded with a pending order, Inventory checks the hold; if expired or missing it re-runs the all-or-nothing reserve for the same lines. If all lines fit, it saves a new hold marked claimed and the order is confirmed; if any line does not fit, nothing is saved, claim result is not claimed, and the order is cancelled (out of stock) and fully refunded.
sonnet.q11: Payment retries the provider call with the same order-id key until the provider accepts (cannot refund twice), then marks the row refunded. The pending refund is tracked in Payment's refund row (pending/refunded, never deleted), and a pending refund raises an alert. Retry count and alert recipient are not stated.
sonnet.q12: OrderConfirmed (published by Order) causes the Cart service to empty the cart; emptying an empty cart does nothing.
